name: Pro-Worker AI Benchmark
description: A benchmark for evaluating whether large language models augment or substitute for human cognition. Measures 11 behavioral dimensions (cognitive forcing, contrastive explanation, skill preservation, draft annotation, uncertainty transparency, complementarity, adversarial resilience, anti-sycophancy, metacognitive calibration, appropriate reliance, ethical surfacing) across 320 prompts organized in three layers (200 single-turn behavioral probes, 16 multi-turn scenarios, 40 adversarial stress tests). Includes 0-3 scoring rubrics, few-shot calibration examples, and evaluation results from 7 LLMs.
citeAs: @inproceedings{proworker2026, title={The Pro-Worker AI Benchmark: Measuring Whether Large Language Models Augment or Replace Human Intelligence}, author={Anonymous}, booktitle={NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations \& Datasets Track}, year={2026}}
rai:dataCollection: Prompts authored by the research team based on realistic professional scenarios across 13 domains. Rubrics developed iteratively from peer-reviewed literature in HCI, labor economics, and human-AI interaction. Model responses generated via Vultr Serverless Inference API. Judge scores produced by 3-model panel (Devstral-2 123B, GPT-oss 120B, Gemma 4 31B) with median aggregation.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmark evaluation of LLM alignment with pro-worker principles. Research on prompt engineering for human-AI augmentation. Training signal for pro-worker RLHF. Comparative evaluation of LLM behavioral patterns beyond task accuracy.
rai:dataLimitations: English-only; may not transfer to languages with different cultural norms around directness and deference. Judge and candidate models partially overlap (documented as self-evaluation bias analysis). Two dimensions (appropriate_reliance, uncertainty_transparency) show lower inter-rater reliability and are flagged for rubric refinement. Benchmark reflects current LLM capabilities and may saturate as models improve.
rai:dataBiases: Rubrics encode a specific theoretical position (pro-worker AI from Bucinca, Acemoglu, Mollick research) that some researchers may contest. Professional scenarios draw from Anglo-American workplace norms. Models evaluated are all open-weight; proprietary models (GPT-4o, Claude) not evaluated due to API tier access constraints.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. All prompts feature fictional scenarios with invented companies, metrics, and situations. No real persons, private health information, or identifiable data.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: provides standardized measurement of whether AI systems preserve human agency and skills. Negative: benchmarks can be overfit to; encourage pairing with human validation studies. The pro-worker framing itself represents a value position about what constitutes good AI behavior, which readers should engage with critically.
